findings.title: Capabilities do not drop ALL
findings.detail: The runtime's default capabilities (CHOWN, SETUID, NET_RAW on many runtimes…) stay enabled.
findings.fix: Add `securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]` and add back only NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed.

findings.title: allowPrivilegeEscalation is not false
findings.detail: A setuid binary in the image could gain more privileges than its parent process.

findings.title: runAsNonRoot is not true
findings.detail: Nothing stops the container from running as root. The image's USER decides, and many images default to root.
findings.fix: Set `securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true` (pod or container) and run the image as a non-zero UID.
findings.reference: PSS Restricted: Running as Non-root; NSA/CISA hardening

findings.title: seccomp profile not set
findings.detail: Without RuntimeDefault, most runtimes run the container with no seccomp filter at all.

findings.title: No memory limit
findings.detail: Without a memory limit the container can use all of the node's memory and get other pods evicted or OOM-killed.
findings.fix: Set `resources.limits.memory`; without it one container can exhaust the node's memory.

findings.title: Service account token is mounted automatically
findings.detail: Every container gets a token for service account `default`; if the app never calls the Kubernetes API, that token is only useful to an attacker.
findings.fix: Set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on the pod (or its ServiceAccount) unless it calls the API.

findings.title: Root filesystem is writable
findings.detail: An attacker who gets code execution can modify binaries and drop tools in the container.
findings.fix: Set `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and mount an emptyDir where the app writes.
findings.reference: NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide: immutable container filesystems

findings.title: No memory request
findings.detail: The scheduler assumes the container needs no memory.
findings.fix: Set `resources.requests.memory` so the scheduler places the pod correctly.

findings.title: No CPU request
findings.detail: The scheduler assumes the container needs no CPU, so it can be starved on a busy node.
findings.fix: Set `resources.requests.cpu`; without it the pod is BestEffort/Burstable and can be starved.

findings.title: No liveness probe
findings.detail: Kubernetes only restarts the container when the process exits, not when it hangs.
findings.fix: Add a `livenessProbe` that detects a wedged process (not a dependency check).

findings.title: No readiness probe
findings.detail: The pod receives traffic as soon as the container starts, before the app is ready.
findings.fix: Add a `readinessProbe` so traffic only reaches ready pods during rollouts.

findings.title: No namespace, or the default namespace
findings.detail: No metadata.namespace: it lands in whatever namespace kubectl is pointed at.
findings.fix: Set `metadata.namespace` to a dedicated namespace (or rely on Kustomize/Helm to set it).

findings.title: No CPU limit
findings.detail: No CPU limit: the container can burst to idle CPU on the node.
findings.fix: Optional: many teams leave CPU unlimited to avoid CFS throttling; set one if your policy requires it.
